recent.author: Ken Snyder
recent.message:
test(sniff): cover primary_layer shallowest-root and enum-order rules

- Add two L1 unit tests covering rules 2 and 3 of the documented `primary_layer()` selection algorithm.
- Rule 2 test: when no layer sits at the repo root, the shallowest nested root wins regardless of authority priority (pnpm at `/repo/apps` beats cargo at `/repo/tools/nested`).
- Rule 3 test: same-depth nested layers tie-break by `MonorepoStandard` declaration order; layers are listed opposite the expected order so the test would fail under iteration/push-order tie-breaking.
- Closes a coverage gap in the existing `primary_layer` test suite, which only exercised rule 1 directly.
- Production code (`primary_layer()` itself) is unchanged.

docs(sniff): add review-1 and review-2 of monorepo-cli plan

- Add review-1.md marking ready: false with a High finding that
  `format_monorepo_label` dropped all but the first orchestrator
  (text surfaces lost user-observable topology information that the
  spec said the unified label helper should carry), and a Medium

  under-tested (no L1 coverage for the "no repo-root layer →
  shallowest root" or "same-depth nested → enum-order tie-break"

- Add review-2.md marking ready: true with no blocking findings,
  confirming `format_monorepo_label` now renders every orchestrator
  in layer order (`Nx + Lerna (using pnpm workspaces)`) with L1
  unit coverage for zero, one, and multiple orchestrators, and
  `RepoInfo::primary_layer()` has L1 coverage for the documented
  fallback cases.
- Both artifacts live in sniff/features/2026-06-16-monorepo-cli/
  alongside plan.md and spec.md, documenting the review process
  for the Monorepo CLI Wiring Cleanup feature.

recent.author: Ken Snyder
recent.message:
feat(sniff-cli): join every monorepo orchestrator in unified label

- format_monorepo_label now joins every orchestrator in layer order with
  " + " instead of dropping all but the first via orchestrators.first().
- A layer can carry multiple orchestrators (e.g. Nx + Lerna over a pnpm
  workspace); the prior behavior silently hid every orchestrator except
  the first, so the CLI surface no longer matched the JSON orchestrators
  array the topology layer emits.
- Doc comment updated to describe the multi-orchestrator format and the
  deterministic order it preserves.
- New monorepo_label test module adds three L1 cases covering zero, one,
  and multiple orchestrators, locking the new join behavior in place.
